purpose: Map pilot lesson topics to official Hall themes without remapping learner achievements or assuming a six-week phase equals a lesson.

lessons.note: Introductions and greetings directly support the identity unit.
Spelling one's name, accents and clarification support identity exchanges.
Family description expands the identity theme through descriptive agreement.
Classroom present tense belongs primarily to the Hall's school/work theme (Unit 02).
Food and café exchanges belong primarily to the Hall's food theme (Unit 03).
The welcome and café mission combines identity, school/work and food. It is not an official Unit 01 final.
Past-event narration directly fits past experiences.
Passé composé and agreement are core supports for past experiences.
Imparfait provides habits, settings and contrast for recounting experiences.
Pronouns help avoid repetition when retelling personal experiences.
Comparing personal narratives fits the first official theme.
The travel notebook reinforces past experiences with a context also associated with later travel problems.

Register and translation shape identity/migration narratives and later literature/film analysis. Pilot teaching model and tasks now explicitly reflect identity and migration narratives; individual drafted assessment items still require independent topic-by-topic review.

Archival, documentary and literary study crosses identity/migration, history/memory and literature/film. Pilot teaching model and tasks now explicitly reflect identity and migration narratives; individual drafted assessment items still require independent topic-by-topic review.
